primary_cause: Evidence is conflicting: June reported sharply higher container rates and strong demand, while July reported falling rates as capacity increased and demand softened. The available evidence does not establish a consistent current industry-wide cycle.
counter_evidence: Container spot rates fell 4% week over week to $4,374 per 40-foot container, with Drewry attributing the decline to increased capacity and easing demand; blank sailings also declined. primary_cause: Capesize demand and constrained vessel availability lifted dry-bulk freight rates, with reported support from strong bulk-commodity exports and iron-ore shipment disruptions. The outlook remains exposed to a potential future supply overhang.
counter_evidence: The dry-bulk supply-demand balance was described as supportive in 2026 but expected to weaken in 2027 as Panamax and Supramax deliveries increase and current geopolitical and weather-related capacity distortions potentially normalize. [Dry Bulk Shipping Faces 2027 Supply Glut: BIMCO Warns Hormuz Rerouting Boost Will Reverse] https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322617/20260801/dry-bulk-shipping-faces-2027-supply-glut-bimco-warns-hormuz-rerouting-boost-will-reverse.htm
source_summary: The Baltic Dry Index rose 5.6% to 2,991 points, extending a four-session gain, while the Capesize market strengthened sharply on tightening Pacific ship availability, disruptions to Brazilian iron-ore exports and expected strong bulk-commodity exports. [Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand] https://gcaptain.com/dry-bulk-shipping-rates-hit-two-year-high-on-capesize-demand/
